name: Gate → RETRY: re-dispatch the developer for a fresh attempt
description:
The retry router (design SB4, group 7D). When check_gate derives RETRY — the attempt was not clean (a failing measurement or a rejecting floor) AND the task's iteration budget still has room (distinct task.attempt.<i> count < task.spec.<i>.budget) — spawn a FRESH developer loop (Amelia) to revise the fix via apply_patch. That fresh loop re-arms the whole chain FOR FREE: it terminates on success → measure (dev-from-task/05, which appends a NEW distinct task.attempt.<i> object, incrementing the count) → floors (06) → gate (07) again, until the task advances or the budget is exhausted (escalate).

⚠ SERIALIZATION INVARIANT (load-bearing, group-7D conformance pin): this rule and dispatch-developer (dev-from-task/04) are the ONLY two rules permitted to spawn a role=developer loop into a run. The gate chain is strictly serial (dispatch → developer → measure → floors → gate → retry), ONE developer loop in flight per task, and this serialization is what guarantees measure and floors evaluated the SAME frozen checkout (it replaced the dropped token handshake — the architect's 7D ruling). A second concurrent developer-spawner would let two attempts race the shared checkout and mis-count the budget. A conformance pin asserts exactly these two spawners.

TRIGGER = the check_gate LOOP terminal via the dev.gate_decision loop marker. Fires on agent.loop.role=coordinator AND dev.gate_decision eq "retry" — a single LITERAL eq (#519-immune), mutually exclusive with the advance/escalate routers on the single decision value.

RUN BINDING: run_scope=inherit reads the gate loop's bare agent.run and binds the fresh developer loop to the same run, so apply_patch targets THIS run's checkout (the same warm sandbox measure re-runs in). related_loops threads the run entity id so Amelia can query_entity the run to re-read the task.spec.

SELF-EXTINGUISHING ONE-SHOT (restart-safe, CRITICAL here): on_enter FIRST stamps dev.routed=$entity.instance on the gate loop, guarded by dev.routed length_eq 0. Unlike the advance router (idempotent add_triple), THIS router's publish_agent is NOT idempotent — a re-fire would spawn a DUPLICATE developer, directly violating the one-in-flight invariant. So the marker (stamped BEFORE the publish, so a publish failure stalls-toward-human rather than duplicating) is load-bearing, not tidiness. A fresh gate loop per attempt carries no dev.routed, so each attempt's gate can retry once.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.developer
on_enter.prompt:
SEMDEV DEVELOPER (Amelia) — your previous attempt at this run's task did NOT pass the sandbox gate (the test failed or a structural floor rejected it). Revise the fix and author a corrected diff.

Your run entity ID is $entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id. Read its state with query_entity(entity_id="$entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id") — the immutable task specs (task.spec.<i>.*) and the recorded measurement/floor findings for your prior attempt. Implement a corrected change, then author it as a unified diff (git format, a/ and b/ prefixes) and record it with apply_patch. The harness re-applies it to the run's checkout and re-measures the real result — you run nothing and claim no outcome. Calling apply_patch completes your turn.

metadata.station: route retry — re-dispatch the developer for a fresh attempt (SB4, 7D)
metadata.trigger_rationale: fires on the check_gate loop's dev.gate_decision marker with a LITERAL eq "retry" — #519-immune, mutually exclusive with advance/escalate.
metadata.serialization_invariant: this rule and dev-from-task/04 (dispatch-developer) are the ONLY sanctioned role=developer spawners (load-bearing, replaces the dropped token handshake — guarantees measure/floors saw the same frozen checkout by keeping ONE developer in flight). A conformance pin asserts exactly these two.
metadata.restart_safe: SELF-EXTINGUISHING via the LOOP-scoped dev.routed marker + length_eq 0 guard, stamped BEFORE the publish. CRITICAL (not tidiness): publish_agent is not idempotent, so a re-fire without the guard spawns a duplicate developer and breaks the one-in-flight invariant.
metadata.budget_note: the budget bound lives in check_gate (distinct task.attempt.<i> count vs task.spec.<i>.budget). This router only fires on the retry decision, so the loop is bounded by construction: at count == budget the gate decides escalate (08c), not retry, and this rule does not fire.
